questions.solution: Commercialization of agriculture signifies the presence of a marketable surplus, where farmers produce more than what is required for their own consumption and can sell the excess in the market. This shift towards producing goods for sale rather than solely for personal consumption reflects increased agricultural productivity and integration into market economies.

The Gulf of Khambhat, the Gulf of Kutch, and the Sundarbans region in India are well-suited for harnessing tidal energy due to their significant tidal movements. In February 2022, the West Bengal government introduced the "Paray Shikshalaya" program, offering open-air classroom sessions for students in grades 1 to 7. This initiative aims to provide an alternative learning environment and mitigate the challenges posed by the COVID-19 pandemic on traditional classroom settings.

Shashi Prabha Dwivedi, as of 2023, holds the distinction of being one of the first women officers to serve as the Director General of Police in Punjab. Her appointment marks a significant milestone in the field of law enforcement, reflecting progress towards gender diversity and inclusivity in senior leadership roles within the Indian Police Service.

The Atal Tunnel, named after former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee, is the longest highway single-tube tunnel in India. It significantly reduces the travel time and distance between Manali and Keylong in Himachal Pradesh, providing all-weather connectivity to the remote regions of the state.

Plutonium, discovered by Glenn T. Seaborg in 1940, serves as a vital heat source in satellites for powering sensitive electrical components. Its radioactive decay produces a steady stream of heat, which is converted into electricity via thermoelectric generators, ensuring reliable power for extended space missions.

A compound characterized as a secondary alcohol features a hydroxy group (-OH) attached to a saturated carbon atom, which in turn is connected to two other carbon atoms. This distinguishes it from primary alcohols, where the carbon is attached to only one other carbon atom, and tertiary alcohols, where the carbon is connected to three other carbon atoms.

Flatworms are a type of endoparasite found in animals. They live inside the bodies of their host organisms, often within the digestive tract or other internal organs, where they derive nutrients and potentially cause harm or disease.

Tughril Beg revolted against Balban, the Sultan of Delhi, in 1279 and established himself as an independent ruler of Bengal. This revolt marked a significant challenge to the authority of the Delhi Sultanate and led to the establishment of a separate ruling dynasty in Bengal.

India won gold in men's hockey at the Olympic Games in the year 1980, held in Moscow, Soviet Union. This victory marked India's eighth gold medal in Olympic hockey, further solidifying its dominance in the sport during that era.

Weathering refers to the natural process of mechanical breakdown and chemical alteration of rocks on the Earth's surface due to atmospheric agents. It leads to the disintegration and decomposition of rocks, ultimately shaping landscapes and contributing to soil formation.

The Lomas Rishi cave, a remarkable example of ancient rock-cut architecture, is situated in the state of Bihar, India. Constructed during the Maurya period, it is part of the Barabar Caves complex, known for their historical and archaeological significance.

In T20 cricket matches, bowlers are limited to delivering a maximum of 4 overs each. This restriction aims to maintain the balance between batting and bowling sides, adding strategic depth to the game, and ensuring equal opportunities for both teams within the shorter format.

questions.solution:
The given sentence is in active voice. In the active voice, the subject (my father) performs the action (is reading) on the object (the newspaper).

questions.question: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. Sanyukta has to bake fifty-one cakes for the anniversary party.

Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

Sanyukta has to bake fifty-one cakes for the anniversary party.

options.text: Fifty-one cakes will be baked by Sanyukta for the anniversary. party.
options.html: Fifty-one cakes will be baked by Sanyukta for the anniversary. party.

options.text: Fifty-one cakes had to be baken by Sanyukta for the anniversary party.
options.html: Fifty-one cakes had to be baken by Sanyukta for the anniversary party.

options.text: Fifty-one cakes have to be baked by Sanyukta for the anniversary party.
options.html: Fifty-one cakes have to be baked by Sanyukta for the anniversary party.

options.text: Fifty-one cakes has to be baked by Sanyukta for the anniversary party.
options.html: Fifty-one cakes has to be baked by Sanyukta for the anniversary party.

questions.solution:
The given sentence is in active voice. In active voice, the subject performs the action expressed by the verb.

Active Voice: Sanyukta (Subject) + has to bake (Verb) + fifty-one cakes (Object).

In a passive voice sentence, the object of the active voice becomes the subject of the passive voice. The action of the active verb becomes the focus, and the doer (subject) may or may not be included. The verb is transformed into the appropriate form of the auxiliary verb "to be" (am/is/are/was/were) followed by the past participle form of the main verb. The subject performing the action can be mentioned using the preposition "by."

Passive Voice: Fifty-one cakes (Object) + have to be baked (To be verb in present tense) + by Sanyukta (Subject)

Hence, (c) is the correct answer.

questions.question: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. It is not a walker's paradise. So walking is not a fashionable pastime here. B. London is known for its hectic face, frenzied movements, high decibels and dust kicked by the speeding vehicles. C. On the contrary, life in the countryside is laid back and easy paced. Unless it is raining, people set out for a walk. D. For these reasons, Max never went out for a walk, nor did anyone ask him to accompany.
questions.questionHtml:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in

the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. It is not a walker's paradise. So walking is not a fashionable pastime here.

B. London is known for its hectic face, frenzied movements, high decibels and dust kicked by the speeding vehicles.

C. On the contrary, life in the countryside is laid back and easy paced. Unless it is raining, people set out for a walk.

D. For these reasons, Max never went out for a walk, nor did anyone ask him to accompany.
questions.solution: After going through all the sentences thoroughly, we can say that B and A form a pair as B describes the bustling and chaotic nature of London and A mentions that walking is not fashionable in London. D should follow A as D indicates Max's aversion to walking in London due to prior mentioned characteristics. Finally, C contrasts life in the countryside with life in the city, highlighting the preference for walks in the countryside. So, the order BADC forms a coherent paragraph. Hence, (b) is the correct answer.

questions.questionHtml:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in

the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. The government's recent efforts have concentrated on strengthening these ties.

B. The textile industry in India is one of the country's oldest, stretching back several centuries.

C. The textile business is immensely diverse, with hand-spun and hand-woven textiles at one end of the spectrum and capital-intensive modern mills at the other.

D. Its tight ties to agriculture (for raw materials such as cotton) and the country's old history and traditions in terms of textiles set it apart from other sectors in the country.
questions.solution: After reading all the sentences thoroughly, we can say that B provides the introduction to the topic. C should be placed next as it expands on the diversity within the textile industry. D should follow C as it further elaborates on the unique characteristics of the Indian textile industry. A is clearly a concluding sentence as it mentions recent government efforts related to the textile industry. So, BCDA forms a coherent paragraph. Hence, (c) is the correct answer.
